sections.heading: About the Commission
sections.intro: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) is a constitutional body established under Article 338 of the Constitution of India with the objective of safeguarding the rights and interests of the Scheduled Castes and the Anglo-Indian community. Its creation reflects the commitment of the framers of the Constitution to ensure social justice, equality, and protection against any form of exploitation or discrimination faced by these historically marginalized communities.

blocks.html: The Commission comprises a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and other Members supported by a Secretariat and specialised wings (Service Safeguards, Development & Welfare, Investigation & Grievance).

items.caption: 28 जून 2026 | चंडीगढ़-- NCSK के उपाध्यक्ष श्री हरदीप सिंह गिल ने चंडीगढ़ सेक्टर-26 स्थित बापूधाम कॉलोनी के भगवान वाल्मीकि आश्रम में वाल्मीकि समाज एवं सफाई कर्मचारियों के साथ प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के 'मन की बात' कार्यक्रम का सामूहिक श्रवण किया। इस अवसर पर समाज में जनभागीदारी, सामाजिक जागरूकता एवं राष्ट्र निर्माण के संकल्प को और मजबूत करने का संदेश दिया गया।

27 जून 2026 | चंडीगढ़-- NCSK के उपाध्यक्ष श्री हरदीप सिंह गिल ने पंजाब के राज्यपाल एवं यूटी प्रशासक श्री गुलाब चंद कटारिया से मुलाकात कर सफाई कर्मचारियों की लंबित मांगों को लेकर ज्ञापन सौंपा। ज्ञापन में नियमितीकरण, पेंशन, सेवानिवृत्ति आयु में वृद्धि, वेतन संबंधी मुद्दों एवं वाल्मीकि भवन हेतु भूमि आवंटन सहित विभिन्न मांगों को प्रमुखता से उठाया गया। राज्यपाल ने संबंधित अधिकारियों के साथ शीघ्र बैठक कर आवश्यक कार्रवाई का आश्वासन दिया।

27 जून 2026 | नई दिल्ली-- राष्ट्रीय सफाई कर्मचारी आयोग के माननीय सदस्य श्री कर्म सिंह कर्मा जी ने मुंडका स्थित मारवाह प्रिंटर फैक्ट्री में सेप्टिक टैंक की सफाई के दौरान 26.06.2026 को जहरीली गैस की चपेट में आकर दिवंगत हुए सफाई कर्मचारी अरुण सिंह, चाँद एवं संदीप के परिजनों से मुलाकात कर शोक संवेदना व्यक्त की। इस अवसर पर एसडीएम मुंडका, एसीपी, एसएचओ एवं तहसीलदार मुंडका भी उपस्थित रहे। आयोग ने पीड़ित परिवारों को तत्काल ₹30 लाख मुआवजा, दोषियों के विरुद्ध सख्त कानूनी कार्रवाई तथा न्याय सुनिश्चित करने के निर्देश दिए।

dr-ambedkar-international-centre.title: Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC)
dr-ambedkar-international-centre.lead: Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), located at 15 Janpath, New Delhi, is a premier autonomous organization under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

sections.heading: About DAIC
sections.intro: The state-of-the-art Centre, spread over approximately 3.25 acres in the heart of Delhi, is housed in a three-storey building comprising the administrative block and other facilities. The Centre was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, on 7 December 2017. The exterior is adorned with a wide variety of green plants that enhance the aesthetics of the place. It features an 18-foot bronze statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, a small Amphitheatre, two Chaitya Arches, two Red Stone Toran Gates, a Buddha Statue, and the imposing Ashoka Stambh on the right façade. The Centre also has a vast circular atrium beneath the central dome, where a grand seated statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar occupies the central space. Information regarding the conduct of programmes and the booking of facilities is available at the reception at DAIC.

sections.heading: About the Corporation
sections.intro:
NSFDC is a Public Sector Undertaking under the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, engaged in promoting economic empowerment of persons belonging to Scheduled Castes by providing concessional financial assistance, skill development and entrepreneurship support.

The Scheduled Castes beneficiaries assisted by NSFDC under concessional financial assistance for self-employment and for pursuing professional/technical educational courses must fall within, presently annual family income of ₹ 5 lakh, as amended from time to time.

blocks.html:
Vision

To be the leading catalyst in the systematic reduction of poverty through the socio-economic development of eligible Scheduled Castes, functioning in an efficient, responsive, and collaborative manner with channelizing agencies and other development partners.

Mission

To promote prosperity among Scheduled Castes by improving the flow of financial assistance through skill development and other innovative initiatives.

The Corporation is headed by Chairman-cum-Managing Director. The corporation is headquartered at Delhi with 4 Liaison Centers at Lucknow, Kolkata, Mumbai and Bengaluru. The total staff strength is 68.

national-safai-karamcharis-finance-devel.title: National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation (NSKFDC)

sections.heading: About the Corporation
sections.intro:
National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation(NSKFDC), A wholly owned Govt. of India Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (M/o SJ&E) was set up on 24th January 1997 as a Company “Not for Profit” under Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956. NSKFDC is in operation since October, 1997, as an Apex Corporation for the all round socio-economic upliftment of the Safai Karamcharis, Scavengers and their dependants throughout India,through various loan and non-loan based schemes.

NSKFDC is the implementing agency for National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE), a Central Sector Scheme jointly implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, and the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. The Scheme has been under implementation since FY 2023–24.

The schemes of NSKFDC are implemented through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) nominated by the State Govts./Union Territory Administrations, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Nationalised Banks. Funds are provided to the SCAs/RRBs/Nationalised Banks for onward disbursement to the target group of NSKFDC at concessional rates of interest for any viable income generating schemes including sanitation related activities.

The details of the various loan and non-loan based schemes implemented by NSKFDC for the socio-economic upliftment of the Safai Karamcharis, Scavengers and their dependants across the country in brief can be found under Schemes and Programmes menu.

sections.heading: About the Corporation
sections.intro:
National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC) is a Govt. of India Undertaking under the aegis of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. NBCFDC was incorporated under Section 25 of the Companies Act 1956 on 13th January 1992 as a Company not for profit with an objective to promote economic and developmental activities for the benefit of Backward Classes and to assist the poorer section of these classes in skill development and self-employment ventures. NBCFDC provides financial assistance through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) nominated by the State Governments/UTs. NBCFDC also provides Micro Financing through SCAs/ Self Help Groups (SHGs). The Corporation can assist a wide range of income generating activities to assist the poorer section of these classes in skill development and self-employment ventures under following broad sectors:

  • a. Agriculture and Allied Activities
  • b. Small Business/Artisan and Traditional Occupation
  • c. Technical and Professional Trades/Courses
  • d. Transport and Service Sector etc.

The Corporation additionally facilitates skill development of poor persons belonging to OBCs, persons of Economically Backward Classes (EBCs), De-notified Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribe, Sr. Citizen, Beggars and Transgender.

blocks.html:
Vision

The Corporation has been established to play a leading role in upliftment of the economic condition of the target group of backward classes.

Mission

To provide concessional financial assistance to the eligible members of the Backward Classes for Self employment ventures and Skill Development Training.
The Commission comprises a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and other Members supported by a Secretariat and specialised wings (Service Safeguards, Development & Welfare, Investigation & Grievance).

sections.heading: About the Board
sections.intro: The Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic, and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC) was constituted on February 21, 2019, to address the unique needs of marginalized communities in India. Historically, these communities faced exclusion and marginalization, including being labeled under the Criminal Tribes Act of 1871. Following the repeal of this Act, DWBDNC continues the government’s efforts towards their rehabilitation and empowerment. We focus on addressing the challenges faced by these communities. Our mission is to provide support and services, promoting social and economic empowerment, and ensuring these communities receive the support they deserve.

blocks.html: The Commission comprises a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and other Members supported by a Secretariat and specialised wings (Service Safeguards, Development & Welfare, Investigation & Grievance).

sections.heading: About NISD
sections.intro:
The National Institute of Social Defence was set up originally as the Central Bureau of Correctional Services in 1961, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, in pursuance of the recommendations emerging at various National Forums. In 1964, the Bureau was transferred to the then Department of Social Security.

Since 1975, the Institute was a subordinate office under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The National Institute of Social Defence has become an Autonomous Body vide Government of India Notification No. 10-3/2000-SD. Vol. II, dated July 15, 2002, and is registered under the Societies Act XXI of 1860 with the Government of NCT, Delhi.

dr-ambedkar-foundation/ambedkar-national.title: Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial
dr-ambedkar-foundation/ambedkar-national.html:
About DANM

  • The national memorial’s Visiting Time is from 10:00 A.M to 07:00 P.M. The memorial is closed on Monday for maintenance.
  • Babasaheb Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, after his resignation from the Union Council of Minister as Minister of Law, vacated his official residence at 1, Harding Avenue, New Delhi and shifted to a Bungalow at 26, Alipur Road, Delhi, on 1st November, 1951 and lived there till he breathed his last on 6th December, 1956
  • The land at 26, Alipur Road, Delhi is considered as a sacred place as a Parinirvan Sthal. There has been a long standing demand from various corners for converting the place into a befitting National Memorial.
  • Setting up of Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial at 26, Alipur Road, Delhi, where Babasaheb Dr. B.R.Ambedkar had breathed his last, was one of the important decisions taken by the Centenary Celebrations Committee of Babasaheb headed by the then Hon’ble Prime Minister of India.
  • The Government of India had initiated the process to reconstruct a well-designed and fully developed Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial at 26, Alipur Road, Delhi. On the advice of Ministry of Urban Development the work had been entrusted to Central Public Works Department (CPWD).
  • The total area of the plot is 7,374 sq metres and the built up area is 4561.62 sq metres excluding basement parking. The memorial consists of one basement for car parking, Lower Ground Floor, Upper Ground Floor and First Floor in accordance with the building by Laws and height restrictions. The total areas are as:

    Sno. Area Area In Square m.
    1. Plot Area 7374.00 sqm
    2. First floor 1362.68 sqm 3. Ground floor 1444.18 sqm 4. Lower ground floor 1485.21 sqm 5. Basement 1248.00 sqm 6. Allied Building 269.75 sqm 7. Total Plinth Area 4561.62 sqm

  • The maximum permissible height is 11 metres. The Memorial will have themed Garden, Entrance Plaza, Surface Parking, Service Area, Meditation Hall, Memorial Plaque, Pavilion and Basement Parking. The other components of the Memorial include a small area at the entrance to the building, with a capacity of 80-100 with chairs for a 5 minute orientation session about the Memorial and an area dedicated for those who want to do meditation.
  • The activities undertaken at the Memorial are (i) organizing Birth and Mahaparinirvan anniversaries (ii) Lectures (iii) discussions (iv) exhibitions (v) cultural activities related to, in particular, young people etc.
  • The Hon’ble Prime Minister laid the foundation stone of Dr. Ambedkar National Memorial, 26, Alipur Road, Delhi and delivered 6th Dr. Ambedkar Memorial Lecture on 21st march, 2016 in the presence of the Hon’ble Minister (SJ&E) and Hon’ble Minister (S&T and Earth Sciences) in a function held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi

dr-ambedkar-foundation/dr-ambedkar-inter.title: Dr. Ambedkar International Center
dr-ambedkar-foundation/dr-ambedkar-inter.html:
About the Project

About DAIC:

The area of state-of-the-art Centre is approximately 3.25 acre in the heart of Delhi and is housed in a 3-storey building that includes the administrative block and other facilities. The exterior holds a wide variety of green plants that add to the aesthetics of the place. It has a 18-feet bronze statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, a small Amphitheatre, two Chitya Arches, two Red Stone Toran Gates, a Buddha Statue and the imposing Ashoka Stambh on the right facade. The centre has a huge circular area on the ground floor under the dome. Here is a large statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar sitting cross-legged on the chair. The information to conduct programmes and to book other facilities is available at the reception at DAIC.
